questions.q: Whose God will Yahweh be?
questions.a: He will be the God of all the clans of Israel.

questions.q: Why did the people of Israel who survived the sword find Yahweh’s favor?
questions.a: They found favor because Yahweh loved them with an everlasting love.

questions.q: What will virgin Israel do after Yahweh builds her up?
questions.a: She will go out with happy dances and have good crops.

questions.q: What will the watchmen in the hills of Ephraim tell the people to do?
questions.a: They will tell the people to go up to Zion, to Yahweh their God.

questions.q: Whom will Yahweh rescue?
questions.a: He will rescue the remnant of Israel who are still alive.

questions.q: Where will Yahweh bring the remnant of Israel back from?
questions.a: He will bring them back from the northern lands and the farthest parts of the earth.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do as he leads his people back?
questions.a: He will lead them along a smooth road to streams of water, where they will not stumble.

questions.q: Who is “the one who scattered Israel”?
questions.a: Yahweh scattered Israel.

questions.q: What will be the signs of Yahweh’s goodness?
questions.a: The people will have plenty of food, wine, oil, and livestock.

questions.q: What will the people do when they stop mourning?
questions.a: They will celebrate.

questions.q: What will Yahweh give the priests?
questions.a: He will give them plenty of food, and he will satisfy his people with good things.

questions.q: Why is there wailing and bitter weeping in Ramah?
questions.a: There is wailing and weeping because Rachel’s children have died.

questions.q: Why should the people stop weeping?
questions.a: Yahweh will bring their descendants back from the enemy’s land.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh have compassion on Ephraim?
questions.a: He will have compassion because Ephraim was ashamed of his sins.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell virgin Israel to do?
questions.a: He tells her to set up signposts to mark the road and return to her cities.

questions.q: What new thing will Yahweh create in the land?
questions.a: The women of Israel will protect the strong warriors.

questions.q: What will the people in the cities of Judah say when Yahweh restores their fortune?
questions.a: They will ask Yahweh to bless the place where he lives, the sacred mountain.

questions.q: Who will live together in the land of Judah and its cities?
questions.a: Farmers and those who move around with their flocks will live there together.

questions.q: Whom will Yahweh satisfy?
questions.a: He will satisfy those who are weary and refresh those who are sorrowful.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah do after he had this dream?
questions.a: He woke up and looked around; his sleep had been very peaceful.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the houses of Israel and Judah that he uprooted and tore down?
questions.a: Yahweh will watch over them so he can build them up and plant them.

questions.q: What is the saying that the people of Israel and Judah will no longer use?
questions.a: The saying is, “Fathers have eaten sour grapes and the children’s teeth are dulled.”

questions.q: Why will the people no longer use that saying?
questions.a: Each man will die for his own sin.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do in the future?
questions.a: He will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

questions.q: What happened to the covenant Yahweh made with the Israelites’ ancestors?
questions.a: The Israelites broke that covenant, even though Yahweh had cared for them like a husband cares for his wife.

questions.q: What is the new covenant that Yahweh will establish with the house of Israel and Judah?
questions.a: The new covenant is this: Yahweh will will cause them to love and believe his teachings in their inner beings. He will be their God, and they will be his people

questions.q: Israel will be a nation as long as what has not vanished?
questions.a: They will be a nation as long as the sun, moon, stars, and sea have not vanished.

questions.q: Yahweh will reject Israel’s descendants only when what two things have happened?
questions.a: Yahweh will reject them only if the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below can be searched out.

questions.q: When the city is rebuilt, will it be bigger or smaller than it was?
questions.a: It will be bigger.

commentary.text: The restoration of Israel. (Jer. 31:1-9) Promises of guidance and happiness; Rachel lamenting. (Jer. 31:10-17) Ephraim laments his errors. (Jer. 31:18-20) The promised Saviour. (Jer. 31:21-26) God's care over the church. (Jer. 31:27-34) Peace and prosperity in gospel time. (Jer. 31:35-40)

Jer. 31:1-9 God assures his people that he will again take them into covenant relation to himself. When brought very low, and difficulties appear, it is good to remember that it has been so with the church formerly. But it is hard under present frowns to take comfort from former smiles; yet it is the happiness of those who, through grace, are interested in the love of God, that it is an everlasting love, from everlasting in the counsels, to everlasting in the continuance. Those whom God loves with this love, he will draw to himself, by the influences of his Spirit upon their souls. When praising God for what he has done, we must call upon him for the favours his church needs and expects. When the Lord calls, we must not plead that we cannot come; for he that calls us, will help us, will strengthen us. The goodness of God shall lead them to repentance. And they shall weep for sin with more bitterness, and more tenderness, when delivered out of their captivity, than when groaning under it. If we take God for our Father, and join the church of the first-born, we shall want nothing that is good for us. These predictions doubtless refer also to a future gathering of the Israelites from all quarters of the globe. And they figuratively describe the conversion of sinners to Christ, and the plain and safe way in which they are led.

Jer. 31:10-17 He that scattered Israel, knows where to find them. It is comfortable to observe the goodness of the Lord in the gifts of providence. But our souls are never valuable as gardens, unless watered with the dews of God's Spirit and grace. A precious promise follows, which will not have full accomplishment except in the heavenly Zion. Let them be satisfied of God's loving-kindness, and they will be satisfied with it, and desire no more to make them happy. Rachel is represented as rising from her grave, and refusing to be comforted, supposing her offspring rooted out. The murder of the children at Bethlehem, by Herod, Matt. 2:16-18, in some degree fulfilled this prediction, but could not be its full meaning. If we have hope in the end, concerning an eternal inheritance, for ourselves and those belonging to us, all temporal afflictions may be borne, and will be for our good.

Jer. 31:18-20 Ephraim (the ten tribes) is weeping for sin. He is angry at himself for his sin, and folly, and frowardness. He finds he cannot, by his own power, keep himself close with God, much less bring himself back when he is revolted. Therefore he prays, Turn thou me, and I shall be turned. His will was bowed to the will of God. When the teaching of God's Spirit went with the corrections of his providence, then the work was done. This is our comfort in affliction, that the Lord thinks upon us. God has mercy in store, rich mercy, sure mercy, suitable mercy, for all who seek him in sincerity.

Jer. 31:21-26 The way from the bondage of sin to the liberty of God's children, is a high-way. It is plain, it is safe; yet none are likely to walk in it, unless they set their hearts towards it. They are encouraged by the promise of a new, unheard-of, extraordinary thing; a creation, a work of Almighty power; the human nature of Christ, formed and prepared by the power of the Holy Ghost: and this is here mentioned as an encouragement to the Jews to return to their own land. And a comfortable prospect is given them of a happy settlement there. Godliness and honesty God has joined: let no man think to put them asunder, or to make the one atone for the want of the other. In the love and favour of God the weary soul shall find rest, and the sorrowful shall find joy. And what can we see with more satisfaction than the good of Jerusalem, and peace upon Israel?

Jer. 31:27-34 The people of God shall become numerous and prosperous. In Heb. 8:8,9, this place is quoted as the sum of the covenant of grace made with believers in Jesus Christ. Not, I will give them a new law; for Christ came not to destroy the law, but to fulfil it; but the law shall be written in their hearts by the finger of the Spirit, as formerly written in the tables of stone. The Lord will, by his grace, make his people willing people in the day of his power. All shall know the Lord; all shall be welcome to the knowledge of God, and shall have the means of that knowledge. There shall be an outpouring of the Holy Spirit, at the time the gospel is published. No man shall finally perish, but for his own sins; none, who is willing to accept of Christ's salvation.

Jer. 31:35-40 As surely as the heavenly bodies will continue their settled course, according to the will of their Creator, to the end of time, and as the raging sea obeys him, so surely will the Jews be continued a separate people. Words can scarcely set forth more strongly the restoration of Israel. The rebuilding of Jerusalem, and its enlargement and establishment, shall be an earnest of the great things God will do for the gospel church. The personal happiness of every true believer, as well as the future restoration of Israel, is secured by promise, covenant, and oath. This Divine love passes knowledge; and to those who take hold upon it, every present mercy is an earnest of salvation.
